summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer, recently found to have liver and bone metastases, was admitted for back pain and urinary incontinence. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection, which was treated with antibiotics, and MRI confirmed extensive osseous metastatic disease without spinal cord compression. Pain was managed with her home opioids and gabapentin. Radiation oncology recommended systemic therapy over radiation due to diffuse disease. She was transitioned to oral antibiotics, started on a bowel regimen due to chronic opioid use, and scheduled for port placement and oncology follow-up to initiate chemotherapy. She improved clinically, with resolution of incontinence and stable vital signs, and was discharged home in stable condition.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct
